title: Fleet Reporting Automation
context: Daily fleet oversight depended on NetSuite exports, GPS logs, maintenance invoices, parts inventory, and separate tracking sheets.
action: Built a unified analytical model with automated ingestion, Power Query transformations, KPI dashboards, and VIN-level history.
impact: Reduced manual report preparation by over 90%, standardized daily oversight, and enabled faster detection of operational anomalies and financial risk.
source: pages/projects/fleet-maintenance-analytics.html — Project Overview, Main Features, Key Components, and Operational Impact

title: Inventory Control Consolidation
context: Inventory status was split across NetSuite, yard sheets, title records, inspections, and deal pipelines, creating conflicting spreadsheets and manual reconciliation.
action: Developed a centralized dashboard with status rules, automated operational blocks, VIN-level drill-through, aging analysis, and yard visibility.
impact: Removed conflicting inventory checks, corrected dozens of availability statuses, exposed documentation and location blocks, and established validated real-time visibility.
source: pages/projects/inventory-control-dashboard.html — Project Overview, Main Features, Key Components, and Operational Impact

title: Warranty Claim Analytics
context: Metro maintenance history was dispersed across records that did not provide a consistent, auditable basis for spare-parts warranty decisions.
action: Designed an Excel model that structured failures by system, dates, responsibility, asset, spare part, station, and contractual criteria.
impact: Created a defensible claim package with stronger traceability and a faster executive submission process for reimbursement or replacement decisions.
source: pages/projects/warranty-claim-analytics-metro-santo-domingo.html — Project Overview, Main Features, Key Components, and Operational Impact

title: Fare Transaction Fraud Detection
context: Transit cards showed balance increases without legitimate recharge transactions, indicating abnormal behavior in the fare-payment workflow.
action: Built a Power BI transaction model and analyzed card lifecycle events, balances, stations, timestamps, recharge activity, and repeated anomaly patterns.
impact: Identified three fraudulent users exploiting a payment-system vulnerability and documented findings for corrective action and security improvements.
source: pages/projects/fare-system-transaction-fraud-detection-metro-santo-domingo.html — Project Overview, Context, Analytical Approach, Outcome, and Tools Used
